what_matters.tag_note: Alphabet · Microsoft · after Wednesday's US close
what_matters.head: Alphabet fell 9.8% in after-hours trading after its profit came in below forecasts. Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours on faster cloud growth. Neither move is in Wednesday's US prices.
what_matters.detail: Alphabet: revenue rose 25% to $127.6B, about what analysts expected, and Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.7B. Earnings per share were $2.67 by the earnings feed's measure, against $3.02 expected; the reported figure, $2.12, includes an $8.7B paper loss on its equity holdings. It spent $51.4B on data centres and equipment in the quarter, and free cash flow was minus $9.1B. It kept its 2026 spending plan of $195–205B and said spending will rise significantly in 2027. Microsoft: revenue was $92.3B against $90.6B expected, and earnings per share $4.89 against $4.72. Azure grew 48%; the company had forecast 44–45% at constant currency, and it now forecasts 49–50% for the December quarter. Spending was $45.2B, lower than analysts expected, after some deliveries of outside data-centre capacity slipped; it expects over $50B next quarter.

what_matters.tag_note: Samsung · results out before the Seoul open
what_matters.head: Samsung made a record KRW 107.4tn operating profit in Q3, almost all of it from chips, but its shares were down 5.4% by 12:05 SGT.
what_matters.detail: Revenue was KRW 195.3tn. The chip division made KRW 106.5tn of operating profit, and the phone, TV and appliance division lost KRW 0.8tn. Net profit, about KRW 75tn, was well below Bloomberg's KRW 89.1tn estimate, and the shareholder-return plan had been expected, Investing.com reported. Samsung plans to return KRW 90–110tn to shareholders for 2026, including a KRW 30tn Q3 dividend; the rest, KRW 55–75tn, will be set at a board meeting in late January. It says it significantly scaled up HBM4 sales but gives no figure, and it expects AI-driven memory demand to far exceed supply in 2027.

what_matters.head: The Fed held its rate at 3.75–4% in a 10–2 vote; both dissenters wanted a quarter-point rise. Tonight brings US GDP and PCE inflation, the ECB, then Amazon, Intel, Sandisk and AXT results.
what_matters.detail: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted for a rise. The next decision is on 9 Dec, with new projections. The 10-year yield rose 5 basis points to 5.05% on the day.

after_data.lead: Aixtron · Q3 statement, Thursday afternoon SGT
after_data.text: Aixtron's statement matched its 15 Oct preliminary figures: orders €275M, revenue €184M, gross margin 48%. Its equipment order backlog reached €549.4M, and optoelectronics made up 68% of the quarter's orders. It kept its 2026 revenue forecast of €560M ± €30M. This is not in Wednesday's Frankfurt price.

recent.headline: Alphabet fell 9.8% in after-hours trading after its profit came in below forecasts. Microsoft rose 2.9% after hours on faster cloud growth. Neither move is in Wednesday's US prices.
SK Hynix's third-quarter revenue passed 100 trillion won for the first time, and operating profit beat forecasts. By 12:05 SGT its shares were up 10.5%, 2.2× their usual day.
Bloom Energy fell 11.2% on Friday, 2.2× its usual day, even though its third-quarter results beat forecasts and it raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
Chip stocks fell hard on Thursday: the chip fund lost 6.8%, 2.7× its usual day, and the Nasdaq 2.6%, its biggest one-day fall since early June.
Meta's revenue beat its own forecast, but a $9.9B legal charge cut earnings per share to $3.83, against the $5.46 analysts expected. The shares rose 2.1% after hours.
